expectations.text: Avoids commodity language and vendor positioning
expectations.evidence: Uses commodity language: 'high-quality photorealistic renders', 'exceptional renders', 'architectural vision'; positions as production vendor; no strategic language present.

expectations.text: Connects to business outcome (sales, decisions, risk, alignment)
expectations.evidence: No connection to business outcomes; offers to 'learn more' and 'customize based on project complexity' but never frames around what problem is solved or what decision is supported.

expectations.text: Positions Rendimension as strategic partner, not vendor
expectations.evidence: Positions as production vendor; opens with deliverables ('5 high-quality photorealistic renders'); explains pricing as 'customized based on project complexity'; vendor positioning throughout.
Completely deliverable-first; leads with 'Proposal Overview' of renders and revisions; discusses 'factors' that affect pricing but never frames outcomes; inverted value hierarchy.

expectations.text: Would pass Hugo's review without edits
expectations.evidence: Would fail Hugo's review; reads as generic vendor proposal; uses 'high-quality renders' and commodity positioning; doesn't establish strategic authority; could come from any visualization studio.
